title: Who Can Be a Paid Caregiver in Missouri CDS? (Family, Friends, and Who Can't)
short_title: Who can be a paid caregiver in Missouri CDS?
description: Can a son, daughter, grandchild, friend or neighbor be paid to care for someone through Missouri's Consumer Directed Services (CDS)? Here's exactly who can be the paid caregiver, who can't (a spouse or a guardian), and what families do when the obvious person can't be paid.
end: Have someone in mind? We'll check the rules with you.

parts.head: Who can be a paid caregiver in Missouri CDS?
parts.sub: Who can, who can't, and what to do instead
parts.text: Can I get paid to take care of my mom? Can a grandson? A neighbor? I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Here's exactly who can, and who can't, be the paid caregiver in Missouri's Consumer Directed Services program, and what to do if the obvious person can't be.

parts.head: Usually someone they already know
parts.sub: An adult son or daughter. A parent of an adult.
parts.text: Good news first. In CDS, the paid caregiver is usually someone the person already knows. An adult son or daughter can be paid. So can a parent caring for an adult child.

parts.head: Family, friends and neighbors
parts.sub: Grandchildren, siblings, in-laws, cousins, church friends
parts.text: So can a grandchild, a grandparent, a brother or sister, a niece or nephew. An in-law, a step-relative, or a cousin. A friend, a neighbor, or someone from church. And even someone you've never met, hired through our caregiver directory.

parts.head: 18+, able to work, passes screening
parts.sub: Plus a one-time state registry fee, about $16
parts.text: Every paid caregiver must be eighteen or older, legally able to work in the US, and able to pass the state's background screening. We run that screening. Missouri also requires every caregiver to register with the Family Care Safety Registry, for a one-time state fee of about sixteen dollars.

parts.head: A spouse
parts.sub: A Missouri rule, with no exception
parts.text: Now, who can't be paid. A spouse. Missouri does not allow a husband or wife to be paid as the caregiver. That's a program rule, not ours, and there's no exception to apply for.

parts.head: A guardian or conservator
parts.sub: And anyone who doesn't pass the screening
parts.text: A court-appointed guardian or conservator can't be paid, either. And anyone who doesn't pass the background screening can't be hired. That's the one thing we can't work around.

parts.head: They stay in charge
parts.sub: Power of attorney: let's look. Guardian: CDS isn't allowed.
parts.text: One more rule is about the person getting care. They have to direct their own care. If they have a power of attorney, that alone doesn't rule anyone out. Have the paperwork handy, and we'll look at it with you. But if a court has given them a guardian or conservator, Missouri doesn't allow them to enroll in CDS. Call us anyway, and we'll talk about what else might fit.

parts.head: What if it's the spouse doing the caring?
parts.sub: Another family member or friend can take the paid hours
parts.text: Here's the hard one. What if the husband or wife is already doing all the caring? The program won't pay them. But what often works is this: an adult child, a brother or sister, a niece or nephew, or a friend takes the paid hours for the tasks they really cover, and the spouse stops carrying it all alone.

parts.head: You can call first. They enroll.
parts.sub: CDS belongs to the person getting care
parts.text: If you're the family member, you're welcome to call us first. That's often how it starts. But CDS belongs to the person getting care. They enroll, they become your employer, and they sign. So we'll need to talk with them, too, and you can be on the call.

parts.head: $15 to $16 an hour, every Thursday
parts.sub: Once they're enrolled and hire you
parts.text: Once they're enrolled, they hire you, we set you up, and you're paid fifteen to sixteen dollars an hour, every Thursday.

parts.head: Make a free caregiver profile
parts.text: Don't have someone to care for, but want the work? Make a free profile at findcdscaregivers.com. It takes about two minutes, no experience is needed, and once your state screening is done, families can ask to meet you.
Have someone in mind? We'll check the rules for your situation. Call us at 417-218-2888, or visit caringcds.com. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Thanks for watching.
